A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates conformity: changing behavior or beliefs to match group pressure. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.

stimulus.body: In a 2007 study with 450 retirees in West Africa, 65% changed an answer to match the group, while 33% held to their initial judgment.

questions.stem: What is the point gap in the 2007 Africa group conformity survey?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 33 percent from 65 percent gives 32 percentage points, the gap reported in the 2007 data from West Africa between the two shares.
questions.hint: Look past the numbers to the relationship they describe.
